newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - IG Metall, employers reach regional wage deal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - IG Metall, employers reach regional wage deal.

text.p: German engineering union IG Metall said on Thursday it had reached a regional wage accord with metal employers and ended a bitter dispute over planned cuts in sick pay.

After 13 hours of talks, negotiators for the engineering industry in the state of Lower Saxony said they had agreed a package maintaining sick pay at 100 percent as well as paying a wage increase of 1.5 percent from April, 1997 and a further rise of 2.5 percent from April 1, 1998.
IG Metall has been at the forefront of opposition to a sick pay cut to 80 percent which was made possible by legislation which came into force in October.
It has staged walkouts involving hundreds of thousands of workers and has threatened to strike.

Talks covering 90,000 metal workers in Lower Saxony had resumed at short notice on Wednesday. National talks collapsed in October and attempts at reaching deals in several other regions have failed recently.
IG Metall chief negotiator Juergen Peters said the deal could, but need not, serve as an example for other regions.
"The accord is a breakthrough in the metal industry but does not have the character of a pilot agreement," Peters told a news conference.
One employer representative said the Lower Saxony agreement could set a precedent for deals to be reached in other German regions.
The chairman of the Lower Saxony metal employers group, Dietrich Kroencke, said he regretted that employers had been unable to seize an opportunity to cut sick pay.
But he added that the deal was a sign that wage bargaining was still possible in Germany.
Under the deal, overtime and overtime bonuses will no longer be taken into account when calculating sick pay.

The deal also covers changes in overtime working and holiday bonuses. The Christmas bonus will be cut to 55 percent of pay for 1997 from 60 percent now and the difference will be used to pay a supplement to the long-term sick.
Workers will also receive a one-off payment of 200 marks covering January, February and March of next year.
The accord on sick pay runs until December 31, 2001. The wage agreement runs until the end of 1998.
